evidence: STRUCTURE SUPPORTS A GRADED SPREAD. (1) tests/scoring.toml:1-11 gates render/constraints at 0.0, weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, floor functional 0.05; tests/tools/score.py:46-48 computes reward = weighted mean when gates and floors pass, so the final reward is a continuous blend of three dimensions, not a single pass/fail. (2) Functional (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml) has 43 binary criteria, aggregation weighted_mean, weights 0.5-2.5 summing 58.5; the largest single criterion is 2.5/58.5 = 4.3% of functional (2.6% of reward), the smallest 0.85%. Polish has 5 binary weighted criteria (weights 3,3,2,1.5,2.5; max share 25%). Visual has 5 likert points=5 criteria with described 1-5 anchors (e.g. hro_vis_type), each 20% of visual. So the reward has fine granularity across many independently observable outcomes. (3) Gates are cheap basics and do not collapse partial apps: hro_gate_render = wrong password refused + Recruiter sign-in shows a usable workspace; hro_gate_shared = open a job (title, team, manager, 2 places) and add one candidate via UI, then an independent Observer context sees that card in Applied. Both preconditions (interview places, Observer role) are public requirements (instruction.md:3 'Interview has a limited number of places per job'; hireops_rules.md:27-28 job fields, :18 Observer row), and the gate allows 'another working staff account' if Observer sign-in fails. The scored prompts' in-dimension gate repeats the same minimal check, so a gate-passing app is not re-zeroed by a stricter hidden gate. (4) Anti-collapse wording: functional prompt.md:13 'Once it succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures and keep successful observations. A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row ... When a setup step fails, set up the same thing again on a new job of your own'; prompt.md:23 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row'; criteria carry ownership notes (e.g. hro_arrive_bottom defers multi-card arrival to hro_bulk_move; hro_candidate_linked 'This row alone owns that link; rows run on his seeded conversation instead are not reduced'; T protocol falls back to Tomas's seeded conversation). polish prompt.md:12 'judge each criterion independently and continue after failures'. This addresses the reference's 'criteria that all depend on one precondition' failure mode. (5) Thought experiments: a plausible partial app (correct board rules and permissions but no live push) loses hro_live_board 2.5, the live halves of hro_msg_exchange 1.5, hro_unread_counts 2, hro_unread_scrolled_up 2, hro_seen 1.5 (~9.5/58.5 functional, ~16%) and polish hro_pol_live_board/hro_pol_live_thread (6/12), landing mid-range rather than at 0 or 1; an app without multi-select loses only the four bulk rows (~7/58.5); a stub that only passes the gates scores near-zero functional and is cut by the 0.05 floor. A conforming alternative (no drag, hidden refused controls, different route names) is explicitly allowed ('dragging ... optional', 'hiding it is optional', 'Discover routes and controls by intent'), so it is not forced to 0. WHY NOT PASS. Row 40 is a measured property (spread across partial-quality apps) and no reward-discrimination measurement exists: raw-evidence-index.json scope says verbatim 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'; its only entries are a scripted golden driver run explicitly 'Not a configured judge run, Oracle grade, model score or judge-duration measurement'. REVIEW_POLICY.md requires a separate hash-bound reward-discrimination record before local clearance. Additionally there is an unmeasured all-or-nothing failure path: test.sh:224-226 'if ! run_suite scored 11100; then exit 0' leaves the gates-time reward.json (reward 0 because the scored suite did not produce data), so if the single functional judge (timeout 9000 in judge.toml, a long protocol Z,S,M,L,C,B,N,T,U,K,R,V,A,D with dozens of independent contexts and replays, run by z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx) or the suite overruns, every app - golden or partial - collapses to 0. The wiring (test.sh, 9000 s functional timeout) is template-controlled and not a task defect, but whether this task's functional workload fits it is unmeasured, and that is exactly what decides whether the designed spread is realised. The prompt's 'NOT EXERCISED - evaluator/tool limitation' binary0 rule also means partial budget exhaustion compresses scores of strong apps toward weaker ones. No defect demonstrated; required runtime evidence missing, hence Not exercised with risk=true.
